# Thermal Teleportation Limits

This repository studies one-copy physical-qubit teleportation using a supplied collective Heisenberg Gibbs state. Read the scientific model before transferring a result between access models or parameter limits.

## Central routes

- Task, input, output, allowed laboratories and charged boundaries: science/model.md
- Exact finite Gibbs spectrum and one-spin partial transpose: science/thermal-spectrum.md
- Complete-protocol fidelity upper bound and explicit all-outcome spin-block decoder: science/teleportation-bounds.md
- Fixed-score cooling order and inherited paired-helper Bell decoder: science/cooling-and-decoding.md
- Uniform finite suppression, ordered optimal-excess logarithmic rate and sufficient joint regime: science/rare-sectors.md
- Singleton helper optimum, symmetry-wide ceiling and fixed disjoint-pair converse: science/helper-access.md
- Physical interpretation and finite worked comparison: science/interpretation.md
- Proof-dependency and reading map: science/README.md
- Attribution and model-level prior comparisons: references/related-work.md
- Primary versions and actual comparison scope: references/source-evidence.md
- Finite reproduction commands, expected checks and limitations: verification/README.md

## Learning route

- Selected educational source, notation translation, a complete two-spin example and the bridge to the proofs: learning/anchor-and-bridge.md
- Thirty shared understanding targets, dependencies and source pointers: learning/milestones.md
- Entry and reading order for that route: learning/README.md

The sole educational anchor is John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018). The spin-sector Gibbs analysis and project-specific theorems are supplied by this repository; the book supports the channel, entanglement and symmetry foundations. Distinguish Watrous's unsquared state fidelity from the pure-state overlap averaged in this teleportation score.

## Essential distinctions

The full Gibbs state is not projected onto spin zero. The Hamiltonian contains the factor 1/N. Every failed filter contributes to the teleportation score. Entanglement onset and a fixed fidelity excess have different temperature scales. Rare-sector operational matching permits a receiver laboratory containing all other source spins, including the fixed output spin. The optimal fidelity need not have an established fixed-b limit: its large-N lower and upper envelopes have the stated outer logarithmic rate. A fixed disjoint helper-pair partition is not an arbitrary two-qubit gate budget. The positive singlet Bell decoder, source model and invariant-spin spectrum are inherited ingredients.
